step1.text:
-- x is runSSZ, y is runSZ; σ₁ is N ↦ s(z), V ↦ s(s(z)), the counter cell ↦ 0
-- hσ: σ₁ gives each of the rule's variables a value of its sort
example : c.WellSorted [Srt.«Nat», Srt.«Nat», KCore.Srt.counter] σ₁ := σ₁_wellSorted
-- hmatch: the left side denotes x (lesson 4)
example : PatVal c σ₁ (.app topLabel [.app Sym.«<k>» [.app kseq [.inj Srt.«State» KCore.Srt.kitem
      (.app Sym.«run» [.as (.app Sym.«s» [.var 0]) 1]), .app dotk []]], .var 2]) runSSZ.val := match_runSSZ
-- hreq: the rule has no requires
example : c.rules[0]?.map (·.req) = some none := rfl
-- heval: the right side has the value y (lesson 5)
example : EvalTerm c σ₁ (.app topLabel [.app Sym.«<k>» [.app kseq [.inj Srt.«State» KCore.Srt.kitem
      (.app Sym.«run» [.app Sym.«pred» [.var 1]]), .app dotk []]], .var 2]) (some runSZ.val) := eval_rhs_runSSZ
-- hprio: every rule of peano has priority 50, so none has a smaller one
example : ∀ r ∈ c.rules, r.prio = 50 := fun _ h => Reach.prio_all h
-- so
example : Step c runSSZ runSZ := step_runSSZ

prio.text:
-- go(d) steps to out(d), by go(X:D) => out(X), priority 40
example : Step c goDcfg outDcfg := step_goD

-- go(X:B) => other(X), priority 50, matches go(d) too (X ↦ d, as a B)…

    (.app KCore.topLabel [(.app Prio.Sym.«<k>» [(.app KCore.kseq [(.app Prio.Sym.«go» [(.var 0)]), (.var 1)])]), (.var 2)])
    (pcfg goD) := rule1_matches_goD
-- …but the rule of priority 40 applies, so it gives no step
example : ¬ Step c goDcfg otherDcfg := not_step_goD_otherD

-- go(b) steps to other(b), by the rule of priority 50: b is not a D
example : Step c goBcfg otherBcfg := step_goB
